title: 'Why did Ben run? That's the big question'
article: Benny Matson ran away from two Vancouver police officers who tried to talk to him outside the Yale Hotel bar on Granville Street.
Ten minutes later, the 49-year-old Burnaby truck driver died in an alley a block away as police restrained him.
No one knows why Matson ran, but yesterday, a coroner's inquest began into what happened on May 12, 2002.
"Why did he run? That's the big question," said Matson's daughter, Julie. "But if the police were pursuing him, why were they going to arrest him? As far as I know, there was no reason."

Police internal investigations have already concluded that the officers who restrained Matson acted appropriately and their use of physical force was reasonable. The regional Crown counsel has also examined the case and no charges have been laid against police.

Nick Sharma, an RCMP officer who was off duty that night, testified that he was at the Yale Hotel with four friends to celebrate his cousin's upcoming marriage. When the group left the bar at about 1:45 a.m., they found Sharma's car boxed in by an illegally parked Harley Davidson in front and another car in back.

Sharma said he leaned over the bike to read the licence plate number, and a woman screamed from a hotel room above the bar. "She said something like, 'You touched that bike, you're f---ing dead!'" he said.

A moment later, a dozen men piled out of the bar doors and Matson and another man charged across the street. Sharma said he pulled out his RCMP badge and told them he didn't touch the bike -- he just wanted to get his car out of the parking space. He said the two men stopped and backed away.

At the same time, two police officers arrived in response to a call about an altercation outside the hotel. At first, the dispatcher said one of the men had a knife, but the information was updated a few minutes later to say there was no knife.
After asking Sharma what was going on, the officers called to Matson and started to approach him. Matson turned and ran back into the bar, Sharma said.

Vancouver lawyer Rick Brooks, who is representing Matson's family, said Matson's heart stopped after he choked on his own vomit. The autopsy report also notes six to eight blows, at least three of which left boot tread marks on Matson's scalp.
"All we know is Benny Matson entered the Yale Hotel as a hale and hearty middle-aged man and 10 minutes later he was dead," Brooks said.
"Why did this happen? What did he do? He committed a minor parking infraction, he ran, and the next thing you know he's dead.
"As far as I know, there's no law against running."
